ui.mesh.mesh_approvals.profile_outcome_a.note: The decision was signed but the write has not happened: approval is not a save.

ui.mesh.mesh_approvals.profile_outcome_d.note: Someone answered no; nothing was written.

ui.mesh.mesh_approvals.profile_outcome_e.tone: Plain, factual; not an error apology
ui.mesh.mesh_approvals.profile_outcome_e.note: The window closed with no answer; nothing was written.

ui.mesh.mesh_approvals.profile_outcome_s.note: A runner stopped before applying; nothing was written.

ui.mesh.mesh_approvals.profile_outcome_u.note: This build cannot name the record's state. Never guess 'saved'.

ui.mesh.mesh_approvals.profile_revert_no.role: disabled-control reason — profile-save consent card revert
ui.mesh.mesh_approvals.profile_revert_no.note: The control is drawn here but this surface has no way to send the answer, so it is disabled with this reason.

ui.mesh.mesh_approvals.profile_revert_re.role: disabled-control reason — profile-save consent card revert
ui.mesh.mesh_approvals.profile_revert_re.note: The control is disabled and no specific reason is known; say that rather than leaving it blank.

ui.mesh.pairing.section.note: Accessible name of the block of device-pairing cards inside the Mesh approvals tray.

ui.mesh.pairing.loading.note: Announced while the app reads open pairing requests.

ui.mesh.pairing.title.inviter.role: card title — mesh pairing card, inviting device
ui.mesh.pairing.title.inviter.note: {peer} = the other device's name (inert text); {network} = mesh network name. Shown on the device that sent the invite.

ui.mesh.pairing.title.joiner.role: card title — mesh pairing card, joining device
ui.mesh.pairing.title.joiner.note: {peer} = the inviting device's name; {network} = network name. Shown on the device that is joining.

ui.mesh.pairing.role.note: The role the joining device will have. Keep read/drive/admin as the product's role words (they are also CLI words); translate only 'as'. Other arm echoes an unknown role verbatim.

ui.mesh.pairing.time_left_minutes.note: Minutes left before the pairing window closes; updates live. Keep short.

ui.mesh.pairing.time_left_seconds.note: Seconds left before the pairing window closes; updates every second. Keep short.

ui.mesh.pairing.code.show.role: label over a six-digit code — mesh pairing card
ui.mesh.pairing.code.show.note: Above THIS device's code; the person reads it here and TYPES it on the other device {peer} (that device's card asks for it). The operator chose 'Show': render it as 'display / read this code out for {peer}', or as 'enter this code on {peer}' where that reads more naturally; either way it must point the reader at the other device, not at this one.

ui.mesh.pairing.code.aria.note: Screen-reader name for the code; {digits} = digits separated by spaces.

ui.mesh.pairing.code.type_label.note: Label of the EMPTY field where the person types the code displayed on the other device {peer}. Must clearly mean 'the code that {peer} shows', not this device's code.

ui.mesh.pairing.code.type_hint.role: helper text under the code field
ui.mesh.pairing.code.type_hint.note: Tells the person to copy the digits from the other device's screen and to confirm only if they came from there.

ui.mesh.pairing.waiting.joiner_types.role: status — inviter card before the other device typed
ui.mesh.pairing.waiting.joiner_types.note: The inviting device waits for {peer} to type this device's code; no action needed yet.

ui.mesh.pairing.waiting.inviter.note: The other device {peer} has not typed this device's code yet, so this device cannot answer yet.

ui.mesh.pairing.waiting.other.role: status — joiner card after a local match
ui.mesh.pairing.waiting.other.note: This device typed the right code; now {peer} must confirm on its side.

ui.mesh.pairing.offers.listed.role: list heading — credentials the other device will share
ui.mesh.pairing.offers.listed.note: Followed by a list of credential names {peer} will share with this device.

ui.mesh.pairing.offers.owner_listed.role: list heading with checkboxes — credentials this device will share
ui.mesh.pairing.offers.owner_listed.note: Followed by checkboxes of credentials this device will share with {peer}; the person may untick items.

ui.mesh.pairing.offers.owner_reduce_only.note: The list can only shrink; nothing outside it will be shared.

ui.mesh.pairing.offers.none.note: The other device offered no credentials in this pairing.

ui.mesh.pairing.offers.absent.note: No offer arrived: the other device is an older version, or its offer did not arrive.

ui.mesh.pairing.offers.owner_none.note: This device will share no credentials in this pairing.

ui.mesh.pairing.offers.owner_peer_older.role: status — peer cannot receive a share list
ui.mesh.pairing.offers.owner_peer_older.note: The joining device is older and cannot be shown which credentials will be shared; sharing can be done after it joins.

ui.mesh.pairing.attempts_left.note: How many wrong codes are still allowed before the pairing is declined.

ui.mesh.pairing.action.admit.note: Admits the other device into the network after the typed code matches. Keep to one short verb.

ui.mesh.pairing.action.confirm.note: Confirms the code the joining device typed and opens the native sheet that joins. The SAME verb as ui.mesh.pairing.sheet.button.join (UX: one joiner verb on card, sheet and retry copy) - use your translation of that key exactly.

ui.mesh.pairing.action.confirming.note: Shown on the button while the answer is checked.

ui.mesh.pairing.action.decline.note: Declines the pairing. Keep to one short verb.

ui.mesh.pairing.action.declining.note: Shown on the decline button while it is sent.

ui.mesh.pairing.error.mismatch.note: The typed code is wrong; the card stays open. Plural arm says how many attempts remain.

ui.mesh.pairing.error.mismatch_spent.role: inline error — wrong code, budget spent
ui.mesh.pairing.error.mismatch_spent.note: Wrong code with no attempts left; the pairing was declined.

ui.mesh.pairing.error.needs_app.note: The answer was refused because only the signed desktop app on this device can approve pairings.

ui.mesh.pairing.error.foreground.role: inline error — window not focused / no click / confirmation stale
ui.mesh.pairing.error.foreground.note: The app only approves when its window is in front and the person pressed the card's button; asks them to do that. {action} names the button they pressed: admit = the 'Admit' button (ui.mesh.pairing.action.admit), confirm = 'Join' (action.confirm), decline = 'Decline' (action.decline). Quote each arm's label EXACTLY as your translation of that key, in your locale's quotation marks; 'other' is the generic 'press the button again'.

ui.mesh.pairing.error.build.role: inline error — this build cannot approve
ui.mesh.pairing.error.build.note: Development builds or tool-driven launches cannot approve pairings; the signed app can.

ui.mesh.pairing.error.expired.note: The pairing window closed. Also used as the countdown text at zero.

ui.mesh.pairing.error.relay.note: The local network service did not answer; trying again is safe.

ui.mesh.pairing.error.read.note: The list of pairing requests could not be read; shown beside an 'Ask again' button.

ui.mesh.pairing.error.unknown.note: Fallback when the refusal carried no sentence.

ui.mesh.pairing.result.joined.note: Shown briefly after the joining device's card closes and the network appears. {network} = network name.

ui.mesh.pairing.result.declined.note: The pairing with {peer} was declined (by this device or the other).

ui.mesh.pairing.result.spent.note: The pairing ended because too many wrong codes were typed.

ui.mesh.pairing.result.expired.note: The pairing window ran out; a new invite is needed. INVITER side (this device made the invite and can start the new one); the joiner's twin is ui.mesh.pairing.result.expired_joiner.

ui.mesh.pairing.result.ended.note: The pairing closed without this device answering (the other side stopped or declined).

ui.mesh.pairing.unavailable.host.note: On Windows/Linux the app cannot approve pairings; only the signed Mac app can.

ui.mesh.pairing.unavailable.no_attestati.note: On a Mac whose approval check did not start, the app cannot approve pairings now.

ui.mesh.pairing.unavailable.fallback_inv.note: Followed by a terminal command (not translated). {peer} = other device's name.

ui.mesh.pairing.unavailable.fallback_joi.note: Followed by a terminal command (not translated) that takes the code shown on {peer} as its argument.

ui.mesh.pairing.result.finished.note: Shown after the joining device's card closes but before the network appears: the other device {peer} has the code and decided; if it admitted this device, the network {network} shows up soon. Do not claim success.

ui.mesh.pairing.expired_hint.inviter.role: hint line on an expired pairing card — this device made the invite
ui.mesh.pairing.expired_hint.inviter.note: Replaces the 'type the six digits' hint once the window ran out. This device is the inviter, so it can start a new invite itself (`lop network invite` or the Mesh tab).

ui.mesh.pairing.expired_hint.joiner.role: hint line on an expired pairing card — this device is joining
ui.mesh.pairing.expired_hint.joiner.note: Replaces the 'type the six digits' hint once the window ran out. A joiner cannot start an invite; the new invite has to be made on the other device {peer} (a device name).

ui.mesh.pairing.result.expired_joiner.role: closing line after a joiner's pairing card expired
ui.mesh.pairing.result.expired_joiner.note: Joiner-side twin of ui.mesh.pairing.result.expired: the window ran out (not declined, not closed without an answer). {peer} is the inviting device's name, where a new invite has to be made.

ui.mesh.pairing.sheet.message.inviter_ad.role: native confirmation sheet — title, inviter admitting a device
ui.mesh.pairing.sheet.message.inviter_ad.note: The macOS app shows this in a native sheet before it admits the other device; the person must press the sheet's Admit button. {peer} = the other device's name (inert text); {network} = mesh network name.

ui.mesh.pairing.sheet.message.inviter_de.role: native confirmation sheet — title, inviter declining a device
ui.mesh.pairing.sheet.message.inviter_de.note: Shown before the inviting device declines the other device's request. {peer} = the other device's name; {network} = mesh network name.

ui.mesh.pairing.sheet.message.joiner_adm.role: native confirmation sheet — title, joiner confirming
ui.mesh.pairing.sheet.message.joiner_adm.note: Shown on the joining device before it confirms the code and joins. {network} = mesh network name; {peer} = the inviting device's name. Matches the card title ui.mesh.pairing.title.joiner ('Joining {network} from {peer}').

ui.mesh.pairing.sheet.message.joiner_dec.role: native confirmation sheet — title, joiner declining
ui.mesh.pairing.sheet.message.joiner_dec.note: Shown on the joining device before it declines the invite. {network} = mesh network name; {peer} = the inviting device's name.

ui.mesh.pairing.sheet.device.role: native confirmation sheet — detail line, device
ui.mesh.pairing.sheet.device.note: Names the other device so the person can check it. {peer} = device name; {id} = its fingerprint or device id (opaque, never translated). Keep the label short; one line of a plain-text list.

ui.mesh.pairing.sheet.device_name_only.role: native confirmation sheet — detail line, device without an id
ui.mesh.pairing.sheet.device_name_only.note: Same as ui.mesh.pairing.sheet.device when no fingerprint or id is known. {peer} = device name.

ui.mesh.pairing.sheet.role.role: native confirmation sheet — detail line, role
ui.mesh.pairing.sheet.role.note: {role} = the role the device gets in the network: a core identifier (read, drive, admin) kept verbatim, like ui.mesh.pairing.role.

ui.mesh.pairing.sheet.code.role: native confirmation sheet — detail line, code
ui.mesh.pairing.sheet.code.note: {code} = the six digits being confirmed, grouped '481 926'. Shown on admit only. Use the same word for the code as the card does.

ui.mesh.pairing.sheet.shares_outgoing.role: native confirmation sheet — detail line, what this device shares
ui.mesh.pairing.sheet.shares_outgoing.note: The exact credentials the inviting device will share. Same wording as ui.mesh.pairing.offers.owner_listed followed by {list}. {peer} = the other device's name; {list} = the credential labels joined by the locale's list format (inert text).

ui.mesh.pairing.sheet.shares_outgoing_no.role: native confirmation sheet — detail line, this device shares nothing
ui.mesh.pairing.sheet.shares_outgoing_no.note: Shown when the inviting device admits with no credentials kept. {peer} = the other device's name.

ui.mesh.pairing.sheet.shares_decline.role: native confirmation sheet — detail line on a decline
ui.mesh.pairing.sheet.shares_decline.note: A decline shares nothing in either direction.

ui.mesh.pairing.sheet.button.admit.role: native sheet button — approve the admit
ui.mesh.pairing.sheet.button.admit.note: The only button that admits the device. Keep it the same verb as ui.mesh.pairing.action.admit.

ui.mesh.pairing.sheet.button.join.note: The only button that confirms the code and joins the network on the joining device. One short verb.

ui.mesh.pairing.sheet.button.decline.role: native sheet button — approve the decline
ui.mesh.pairing.sheet.button.decline.note: The only button that sends the decline. Same verb as ui.mesh.pairing.action.decline.

ui.mesh.pairing.sheet.button.cancel.note: Closes the sheet; nothing is sent. Also what Return and Escape press. Use the platform's usual Cancel word.

ui.mesh.pairing.error.closed.note: Core refused a duplicate answer (409 pairing_answered) or the card closed while the person answered: the pairing was answered elsewhere or ended. Not an error to retry; nothing was recorded from this answer.

ui.mesh.pairing.error.changed.role: inline error — pairing changed during the answer
ui.mesh.pairing.error.changed.note: The card moved to a new step, or its details changed, while the native sheet was open, so the approval was not used. {action} names the button to press again: admit = 'Admit' (ui.mesh.pairing.action.admit), confirm = 'Join' (action.confirm), decline = 'Decline' (action.decline). Quote each arm's label EXACTLY as your translation of that key, as in ui.mesh.pairing.error.foreground; 'other' is the generic 'press the button again'.

ui.mesh.pairing.sheet.share_item.role: native confirmation sheet — one shared credential
ui.mesh.pairing.sheet.share_item.note: One item in the sheet's share list. {label} = core's masked account label (e.g. 'OpenAI — sk-…abcd'); {key} = core's identifier for the credential (e.g. 'openai'), shown so two credentials with the same masked label read differently. Keep both placeholders; only the brackets/punctuation are yours. Both are inert text, never translated.

ui.mesh.pairing.sheet.offers_incoming.role: native confirmation sheet — detail line, what the peer offers
ui.mesh.pairing.sheet.offers_incoming.note: On the JOINING device: the credentials the inviting device OFFERS. An offer, not a promise - the inviter can still remove items when it admits (see offers_final_choice). Do not word it as 'will share'. {peer} = the inviting device's name; {list} = items joined by the locale's list format.

ui.mesh.pairing.sheet.offers_incoming_no.role: native confirmation sheet — detail line, the peer offers nothing
ui.mesh.pairing.sheet.offers_incoming_no.note: On the joining device when the inviter offered no credentials (or its offer did not arrive). An offer statement, not a grant. {peer} = the inviting device's name.

ui.mesh.pairing.sheet.offers_final_choic.role: native confirmation sheet — detail line after the offer list
ui.mesh.pairing.sheet.offers_final_choic.note: Follows offers_incoming: the inviting device ({peer}) decides at the end which of the offered credentials it actually shares; it can only remove items, never add.

ui.mesh.pairing.action.waiting_confirmat.note: Shown on the pressed button (Admit/Join/Decline) while the app's native confirmation sheet is open and the person has not answered it yet. Must NOT say the action is happening (not 'Declining…'): nothing is decided until they press the sheet's button.

ui.mesh.pairing.error.devtools.role: inline error — DevTools or a debugger is attached
ui.mesh.pairing.error.devtools.note: Pairings are approved only while no DevTools window or debugger is attached to the app window. Tells the person to close it and press again. {action} names the button they pressed: admit = 'Admit' (ui.mesh.pairing.action.admit), confirm = 'Join' (action.confirm), decline = 'Decline' (action.decline). Quote each arm's label EXACTLY as your translation of that key, as in ui.mesh.pairing.error.foreground; 'other' is the generic 'press the button again'.

ui.mesh.pairing.error.sheet_open.role: inline error — another confirmation is open
ui.mesh.pairing.error.sheet_open.note: Another pairing's native confirmation sheet is already open; this press opened none. Tells the person to finish (answer or cancel) that open confirmation first, then press again. {action} as in ui.mesh.pairing.error.devtools: quote each arm's label exactly as your translation of that action key.
